clue.text: Some crazes that will produce enthusiasm

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A remark that fads tend to stir up eagerness in people.
explanation.definitionFit: Zest is keen eagerness or gusto, a close synonym; the definition reads as 'that which will produce' the quality.

clue.text: Historic city mostly held in regard, looking back

indicators.note: held in says the shortened city sits inside the word for regard

parts.note: to hold someone in regard is to hold them in respect

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all of the word, so its final letter is lost

parts.note: Troy, the ancient city of the Trojan War

explanation.surface: A remark about how an ancient city is largely esteemed when people review the past.
explanation.walkthrough: TROY 'mostly' is TRO, which is 'held in' RESPECT.
explanation.definitionFit: A retrospect is a survey of past events, a backward glance, as in the phrase 'in retrospect'.

clue.text: Difficult situation: spot disheartened bridge partners

indicators.note: disheartened means losing the heart, the middle letters, of the word spot

parts.note: in bridge East and West play as partners, abbreviated E and W

explanation.surface: A bridge pair, dismayed at being caught in a tight spot, find themselves in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disheartened' takes the middle PO out of SPOT, leaving ST.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a stew is an idiom for being agitated or in a predicament.

clue.text: Rude and simple countryman cruelly dismissing son

indicators.note: cruelly suggests the words are treated roughly and mangled into a new order
dismissing says one letter is sent away from the mix

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A rustic simpleton is harshly treated and his son sent off, which is impolite.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the S of 'son' from SIMPLE COUNTRYMAN and rearrange the remaining fifteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncomplimentary remarks are disparaging or insulting, which is what rude speech can be.

clue.text: More than one church property that is included in church indicators

parts.note: CE stands for Church of England

indicators.note: included in says these two letters sit within the word for indicators

parts.note: meters are gauges that indicate a reading
i.e. is the Latin abbreviation for 'that is'

explanation.surface: A dry note about plural church holdings being listed among ecclesiastical signposts.
explanation.definitionFit: Graveyards are often owned by a parish, so burial grounds count as land held by a church.

clue.text: A post I shall abandon, turning up as priest

indicators.note: in a down answer, turning up means the letters are read from bottom to top, reversed
'I shall abandon' is read as the letter I leaving the word, a future-tense deletion signal

parts.note: post is letters delivered, mail
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone quits a job and climbs the ladder to become a cleric.
explanation.walkthrough: A MAIL loses I to give AMAL, which 'turning up' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: A lama is a Buddhist monk or spiritual teacher in Tibet.

clue.text: A long-established driver of industry, were wealth to be redistributed

indicators.note: redistributed means shared out afresh, so the letters are dealt into a new order

explanation.surface: A political musing on what powered the economy if riches were spread around.
explanation.definitionFit: Mills were powered by a wheel turned by flowing water long before steam, an early engine of manufacturing.

clue.text: Salesperson right to avoid door, offering contrition

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative

indicators.note: to avoid says the letter keeps out of the word for door

parts.note: a door is an entrance

explanation.surface: A door-to-door seller shown the door, offering an apology.
explanation.definitionFit: Repentance is sincere regret for wrongdoing, which is what contrition means.

clue.text: Novel plot suppressed by a woman

indicators.note: suppressed by says the plot is held down inside the other letters

parts.note: a dame is a woman
a bed is a plot of garden ground

explanation.surface: A woman stifles the storyline of a new book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like an adjective for plot, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam Bede is George Eliot's first full-length work of fiction, published in 1859.

clue.text: Celebrity finally dabbling in wrong aspect of astrology

parts.note: a star is a celebrity

indicators.note: in says that letter goes inside the word for wrong

parts.note: a sin is a wrong

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of the word dabbling

explanation.surface: A famous person ends up wrongly meddling in horoscopes.
explanation.definitionFit: A zodiac sign such as Leo is a basic element of astrology, assigned by birth date.

clue.text: Leaks not initially seen in ship one sells complete?

indicators.note: seen in says the shortened word sits inside the ship

parts.note: a whaler is a ship used for hunting whales

indicators.note: not initially means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: leaks are holes

explanation.surface: A leaky vessel, with a vendor of entire goods aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition jokes that the word splits as whole plus saler, someone who sells things complete; the question mark flags that playful reading.
explanation.definitionFit: A wholesaler sells goods in bulk to retailers; the question mark flags the punning split into whole plus seller.

clue.text: Hard to engage in a job with some rigging, turning to address someone else

parts.note: a post is a job

indicators.note: to engage in says the letter is meshed inside the word for rigging

parts.note: rope is part of a ship's rigging
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone struggles with a sailing job and turns to talk to another person.
explanation.definitionFit: In rhetoric an apostrophe is a digression where the speaker breaks off to speak to an absent person or thing.

clue.text: Verse form — write dull conclusion? Not conclusion

parts.note: to pen is to write
tame means dull, unexciting

indicators.note: 'Not conclusion' means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a term is an end or limit, a conclusion

explanation.surface: A poet asks whether to write a flat ending, then decides against one.
explanation.walkthrough: TERM loses its last letter, leaving TER.
explanation.definitionFit: A pentameter is a line of five metrical feet, the metre of much English poetry.

clue.text: Wild and very keen to bring in one expert

indicators.note: to bring in says the keen word takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: raring, as in raring to go, means very eager
I is the Roman numeral one
a pro is an expert

explanation.definitionFit: Rip-roaring means boisterous and uproarious, an informal near-synonym of riotous behaviour.

clue.text: Couple moving west, joining new community

indicators.note: in an across answer west is leftwards, so one letter shifts towards the front

parts.note: a couple is two

explanation.surface: A pair relocate westward and join a fresh settlement.
explanation.walkthrough: In TWO the O 'moving west' steps left past the W, giving TOW.
explanation.definitionFit: A town is a settlement where people live together, a community larger than a village.

clue.text: Intruder? In Paris, very unfashionable end for flâneur

parts.note: très is French for very
passé means out of fashion

indicators.note: end for picks the closing letter of the word flâneur

explanation.surface: A Parisian idler, very out of date, may be an unwelcome visitor.
explanation.walkthrough: A flâneur is a man who strolls about idly observing city life.
explanation.definitionFit: A trespasser is someone who enters land without permission, an intruder.

clue.text: Delivering pure half-cut diamonds (though unable to buy them?)

indicators.note: half-cut is slang for drunk, so the letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: the fodder, taken as written
D is the abbreviation for diamonds in card games

explanation.surface: Supplying flawless partly cut gems to those who could never afford them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-cut' seems to describe partly polished diamonds, but it means tipsy and signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Poor people lack the money for luxuries like jewels; the question mark marks this as an illustrative, not dictionary, definition.

clue.text: Nuts — some parts a man held back?

indicators.note: held back means the run is read in reverse order

parts.note: the hiding place, taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: Mast is the fallen nuts of beech, oak and similar trees, food for pigs.
explanation.definitionFit: Mast is the collective name for tree fruits such as beechnuts and acorns lying on a forest floor.

clue.text: Deliveries with flexibility? More than you need

explanation.surface: A shipping firm asks whether its deliveries can be adaptable.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six balls bowled in succession.
explanation.definitionFit: An oversupply is an excess, a glut beyond what is required.

clue.text: Well-known civil engineer: source of annoyance in a lot of English city

explanation.walkthrough: Leeds is a large city in Yorkshire, northern England; 'a lot of' it means dropping its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Celebrated means famous and widely acclaimed, much the same as being familiar to the public.

clue.text: Energy certainly seen in parts of storms

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy
yes, certainly, as an affirmation

explanation.surface: Power is surely present in sections of a tempest.
explanation.definitionFit: The calm centre of a hurricane is called its eye, so several of them belong to several cyclones.

clue.text: Provide military men an opening

parts.note: to do, as in 'we do lunches', is to provide
OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: An instruction to give troops a chance or a gap.
explanation.definitionFit: A door is an entrance, a gap in a wall for passing through; figuratively also a chance.

clue.text: See 10
Pull up around front of store in wind

in a down answer up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to tug is to pull

indicators.note: front of picks the opening letter of the word store

explanation.surface: Someone stops beside a shop in a breeze.
explanation.definitionFit: A gust is a sudden strong rush of air, a burst of breeze.

clue.text: See 9
Work done on pylons with care: it presents the likelihood of dropping off

definitions.text: it presents the likelihood of dropping off

indicators.note: work done on suggests the letters are worked over and reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: Engineers carefully maintain electricity pylons, mindful of the risk of falling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping off' suggests a fall from a pylon, but it means falling asleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Narcolepsy is a disorder causing sudden uncontrollable bouts of sleep.
